lesson.title: Huge changes in Libyan health care: reading
lesson.title_ar: تحوّلات كبرى في الرعاية الصحية بليبيا (1): قراءة سيرة د. سليمان بدوي وتتبع التواريخ الخمسة

lines: Huge changes in Libyan health care   6.8 6.9
Read the title of the page, the title of the magazine article and the introduction to the article. What do you think the article will be about?
Now read the text. What important things happened in Dr Badawi's life in 1960, 1967, 1969, 1973, and 1987?
Dr Suleiman Badawi, Senior Surgeon at Tripoli Central Hospital since 1987, looks back on his life in the Libyan Republic.

I remember the day in 1960 when I decided to become a doctor. I was 16, and two months earlier a good friend of mine, Sadiq, had died of tuberculosis. Now it seemed my younger sister, Fareeda, was going to die too. She had measles, and her temperature was very high. We knew measles was easy to cure - with proper medical care. But the nearest doctor was 200 kilometres away. I felt very angry as we sat with Fareeda. 'Why should good people like Sadiq and Fareeda die?' I asked myself. Disease and death were common in our little country town, where there were no medical facilities at all.

Thanks be to Allah, Fareeda's temperature began to go down the next day, and she slowly got better. However, I was still angry. 'This can't go on', I thought. 'There should be medical help for everyone, not just for a few people in the cities.' That was the day my future was decided.

At that time, there were no training facilities for doctors in Libya, and I had to go to Cairo. Two years after qualifying, in 1969, when I was completing further training in a large hospital in Alexandria, news of the new Republic came.

The Republic put people at the centre of society. And for a better society, everybody needed good health care. This was exactly what I believed! The situation soon began to improve and now we have more doctors for every 1,000 patients than almost anywhere in the world.

In the old days, trachoma was a terrible disease that made many people blind. As an eye surgeon. I was extremely interested in this area of medicine. It was a great moment in my life when I was asked to run the new Trachoma Centre in Benghazi in 1973.

It is wonderful that we now have good health care, with trained medical staff in health centres and hospitals everywhere. Through hard work, we have at last stopped the terrible diseases of yesterday - malaria, tuberculosis and trachoma. I am only sorry that Sadiq cannot be here to see all these changes.
Imagine that you have been told to chose one of the jobs that you have read about in the last two lessons. Which would it be, and why? Which would you not want to do?
Now do activities A to D in the Workbook.

blocks.edu_note_html:
ملاحظات نقل حرفي واستنتاج تاريخي (PB p. 47):
1) في الفقرة الخامسة طُبعت نقطة بدل الفاصلة بعد: As an eye surgeon. I was...، وفي سؤال النقاش أسفل الصفحة طُبعت to chose بدل to choose، وقد حُفظت الصيغ المطبوعة حرفياً.
2) تاريخ 1967 غير مكتوب رقمياً في النص، بل يُستنتج حسابياً من جملة: Two years after qualifying, in 1969 ← أي 1969 - 2 = 1967 (سنة تخرّجه طبيباً!).

interactive_spot.label: الخط الزمني لمحطات حياة د. سليمان بدوي (1960–1987)

simple_explain.html:
• 1960: وفاة صديقه صادق بالسل، ومرض أخته فريدة بالحصبة، وقراره (وهو في السادسة عشرة) أن يصبح طبيباً.
  • 1967 (مستنتج): تخرّجه وحصوله على مؤهل الطب (Two years after qualifying, in 1969).
  • 1969: سماع خبر قيام الجمهورية الجديدة أثناء تدريبه العالي بالإسكندرية.
  • 1973: تولّيه إدارة مركز التراخوما الجديد في بنغازي كجراح عيون.
  • 1987: عمله كبير الجراحين في مستشفى طرابلس المركزي (Senior Surgeon since 1987).

example.html: Predicting before reading: From the title 'Huge changes in Libyan health care' and the subtitle 'Senior Surgeon... looks back on his life', we expect a comparison between poor medical care in the past and strong medical services today.

activities.prompt_literal: Now read the text. What important things happened in Dr Badawi's life in 1960, 1967, 1969, 1973, and 1987?
activities.prompt_ar: حل أسئلة التوقّع والخط الزمني للسنوات الخمس في PB ص 47:

items.model_answer: Aged 16, his friend Sadiq died of tuberculosis and his younger sister Fareeda nearly died of measles (though she recovered); Suleiman decided to become a doctor.
He qualified as a doctor (deduced from 'Two years after qualifying, in 1969').
While completing further training in a large hospital in Alexandria, news of the new Libyan Republic came (and he returned home as soon as he could).
As an eye surgeon, he was asked to run the new Trachoma Centre in Benghazi.
He became Senior Surgeon at Tripoli Central Hospital (since 1987).

hints: لا تبحث عن الرقم 1967 مكتوباً حرفياً؛ بل اطرح سنتين من 1969: Two years after qualifying, in 1969.

activities.prompt_literal: Imagine that you have been told to chose one of the jobs that you have read about in the last two lessons. Which would it be, and why? Which would you not want to do?
activities.prompt_ar: خطة النقاش المقارن لاختيار إحدى وظائف الخدمة العامة من درسي 6.7 و6.8 (PB ص 47):
activities.guidance_literal: 1 Job chosen + reasons (like planning officer / district nurse / eye surgeon) · 2 Job not wanted + reasons

steps.placeholder: I would choose to be an eye surgeon like Dr Badawi because I could save people from going blind and help improve health care in my country.
I would not want to be a district nurse travelling between remote mountain villages in emergencies because the roads can be hard and there is a lot of pressure during serious cases.

hints: حُفظ الفعل 'to chose' المطبوع في النص الأصلي حرفياً، والصواب الإملائي 'to choose'.

questions.stem: In what year did Dr Badawi qualify as a doctor according to the information on PB page 47?

options.why_wrong: في 1960 كان عمره 16 عاماً وقرر حينها فقط أن يدرس الطب.
في 1969 كان قد مرّ سنتان بالفعل على تخرجه طبيباً.
في 1973 تولى إدارة مركز التراخوما في بنغازي.

hints: اقرأ: Two years after qualifying, in 1969.
questions.explain: إذا كان عام 1969 بعد عامين من تخرجه، فقد تخرّج في عام 1967.

questions.stem: Which disease made many people blind in 'the old days' and led Dr Badawi to run a centre in Benghazi?

options.why_wrong: الحصبة (measles) هي المرض الذي أصاب أخته فريدة عام 1960.
السل (tuberculosis) هو المرض الذي توفي به صديقه صادق.
الملاريا ذُكرت في آخر الفقرة ضمن الأمراض التي أوقفتها الرعاية الحديثة، لكنه تخصص جراح عيون في التراخوما.

hints: ابحث عن الجملة التي تضم كلمات blind وeye surgeon.
questions.explain: التراخوما مرض في العين يسبب العمى، وقد تولى د. سليمان إدارة مركز التراخوما ببنغازي عام 1973.
